mechanism_claims.claim_text: Ps series peptides directly disrupt bacterial/model membranes more strongly than Pro-substituted Ps-P analogues, supported by calcein dye leakage, E. coli depolarization, NPN uptake, ONPG hydrolysis, and S. aureus permeability assays.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Ps series peptides, especially Ps, Ps-K18, and Ps-K14-K18
mechanism_claims.limitations: Ps-P analogues are explicitly bounded as lower membrane-permeabilizing and possible intracellular-target candidates; exact intracellular target is not established in this paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Ps and Ps-K18 inhibit LPS-stimulated inflammatory readouts in RAW264.7 macrophages and dendritic cells; main-text exact values support 20 μM NO inhibition for Ps and Ps-K18 and cytokine/protein suppression context.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Anti-inflammatory activity is not promoted for Ps-P analogues; source states Ps-P analogues did not inhibit NO production.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Bio-layer interferometry supports direct TLR4 binding by Ps, Ps-K18, and Ps-K14-K18 with reported affinities of 0.8, 1.5, and 6.9 μM; peptides did not bind MD2 in the reported local source text.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Ps, Ps-K18, and Ps-K14-K18 TLR4 binding
mechanism_claims.limitations: The proposed TLR4-MD-2_LPS complex inhibition is a mechanistic interpretation from TLR4 binding plus downstream assays; direct complex-inhibition quantification is not overextended beyond the source wording.
